question: During the exchange of views between Commissioner Roswall and Parliament’s Environment, Climate and Food Safety (ENVI) Committee on 1 June 2026 on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, several Members raised concerns about the recent killing of hundreds of dolphins in the Faroe Islands.

The Commissioner stated that, although she knew the Faroe Islands from previous responsibilities, she was not familiar with this issue and that Members would soon receive a reply to the letter sent on the matter. 1.

Given that the hunting of dolphins and other cetaceans in the Faroe Islands is a longstanding and widely documented practice that has attracted international attention for decades, what assessment has the Commission made of this issue and its implications for biodiversity conservation and animal welfare?

How does the Commission ensure that concerns raised repeatedly by Members of Parliament on matters related to biodiversity conservation are adequately reflected in its engagement with relevant international partners and stakeholders?

What procedures are in place to ensure that Commissioners and their services are sufficiently briefed on issues that have been raised by Parliament in advance of committee exchanges, and how were these procedures applied in relation to the concerns regarding cetacean hunts in the Faroe Islands?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2026) The Commission acknowledges the strong public concern regarding the hunting of dolphins and other cetaceans in the Faroe Islands.

It attaches importance to cetacean conservation and animal welfare and raises these concerns with the Faroese authorities, including through annual consultations under the Memorandum of Understanding on Enhanced Cooperation between the EU and the Government of the Faroe Islands1.

The Commission is committed to continuing a constructive dialogue with the European Parliament and to ensuring that concerns raised by the European Parliament and its Members are taken duly into account, also through welcoming Members of the European Parliament as observers in the delegations to the relevant international conventions.

The Commission will also continue to engage with all partners, exchange scientific knowledge and promote cooperation to advance shared biodiversity conservation objectives in bilateral dialogues and relevant multilateral fora, including on the issues mentioned above.

In line with the Commission's 2024 Working Methods2, Commissioners, their Cabinets and the relevant services maintain regular exchanges of information to ensure that Commissioners are appropriately briefed for their engagement with the European Parliament.

This includes the sharing of accurate and up-to-date information on issues raised by Members of the European Parliament, including in committee activities and parliamentary questions. These arrangements were applied in preparation for the Commissioner's exchange of views with the European Parliament’s Environment, Climate and Food Safety Committee.
